changes.ink: The last tall crossed stroke is t, followed only by its short exit stroke. There is no separate final e loop and no accent above the preceding e.
The middle of the word has two adjacent tall loops, then a low terminal stroke; no final i dot is visible. These are the l-l strokes of celle, not a u-i ending.
Exactly two parallel horizontal strokes are written between la and application. The word même is not inked.
The last t has a tall upright and short terminal foot; there is a gap before par with no additional e. The two map expressions and their ordinary full arrowheads were read in the same crop.

There is a distinct small raised looped character at the upper right of A, separate from the A strokes and the following set-difference sign. Its compact double-loop/tail shape suggests a, but the exact superscript identity is not fully secure. Plain A omits visible ink. Blind audit admits e and cramped 2 as additional candidates for the compact raised form.

The old word under the strike begins with the long q descender and has later tall strokes consistent with quadratiques. The strike and right-edge compression obscure enough internal/terminal letters that complete certainty is unwarranted. The live doubles is above it. The blind quadruples proposal remains a possible alternative under the heavy strike.
The initial tall crossed t is followed by r/o-like strokes and the short i mark before the ending; there is no initial d-e-u-x sequence.
The next baseline begins with the full word remarquable, including its q descender and final b/l-like tall strokes, before de and the quoted phrase.
Each side of the phrase carries two short high ticks. There are no angle-shaped guillemets. The comma after the closing quotation marks remains live.
The word ends with one tall l and its low exit e; there is no intervening i-s-é sequence between normal and its ending.

The crossed short word has a q loop with a long descender and the following u/i strokes. The strike is confined to that word; contenant begins live on the next baseline. Blind audit: the q-like opening matches live qui below, but the crossed u/i bodies cannot all be certified; pour is a less compatible comparison candidate.
The next baseline opens with a tall looped l, an i dot and the pair of low s strokes ending in es. This word is not crossed; the small separate cancellation follows it.

notes: Only packet 147_scan092 and the shared rules/workflow/notation were consulted. The original page and both native full-resolution halves were read line by line against C and H; every created crop was visually inspected. No OCR, external sources or TeX compilation was used.

Twelve local crops were made once from the original 1690 × 2358 image, all unrotated. Pillow autocontrast, LANCZOS enlargement (2800 pixels wide, except folio 2400) and mild UnsharpMask were used for legibility. Original boxes are recorded in the individual entries.
The top numeral 45 has the main dark ink and position of an authorial page number. The bottom-left 91 is much paler and smaller; its hand is not securely attributed, so it remains marginal foliation.
The opening is transcribed complet … celle … induit. These are the separately observed forms; no grammatical agreement has been normalized and no missing prior noun is inferred from another page.
The two horizontal strokes before application are the abbreviation =. H's même is an expansion, whereas the words application genre themselves agree with the visible ink.

The first normalization expression has additional raised ink after A. It is preserved locally as a suggested superscript a rather than silently omitted. The later two expressions J = A minus A-prime and 2 Card(A minus A-prime) have plain A. No mathematical repair is made to reconcile this variation.

The page describes a third marked set as the inverse image tilde J of J = A minus A-prime, asserts its cardinality is twice Card(A minus A-prime), and expresses the curves using Y and the indicated sigma quotients. These are the source's assertions; no independent proof is claimed.

The two insertion attachments were checked separately: doubles replaces the cancelled adjective; tilde J names l'image inverse and is inserted immediately before de J. Neither insertion is itself cancelled.

There are four separate cancellations: the old node adjective, E after the J formula, qui after Y, and the small letter before tilde J disjoint I. The comma before cancelled E, and the adjective lisses before the last deletion, remain live.
The accent over the X-prime in the definition line has been retraced but remains visible. It is transcribed as a hat; there is no basis to invent a separate deleted expression from the overtracing.

The final sentence reads Ceci étant, au lieu d' followed by the high-double-quoted word oublier. It continues unfinished after pts marqués at the page edge; no ending punctuation or continuation from another page is supplied.

H's editorial page note is not manuscript text. Differences between hat/widehat, tilde/widetilde, mathematical operator formatting, spacing, and the order of deletion/addition wrappers do not by themselves constitute textual errors. The mechanically listed comma after 2 is only H's thin-space command.
No targeted proof check, independent re-proof, computation or formal certificate was performed in this first-reader pass.

The small far-right mark following the first (Y minus I)/sigma denominator is retained as a sentence comma at medium confidence: its bowed turn resembles the clearly written comma after the next quotient formula, whereas the visible local primes are shorter, straighter uprights. It is not classified by the expected mathematics. The blind box includes the full formula and the edge mark.

The sigma-definition blind box begins at y=1570, slightly above the inspected local crop (y=1588), to include the very top of the first quotient formula cleanly. Its remaining bounds are the same. No new first-pass crop was made.

Blind review retains complet without normalizing the agreement. It broadens the raised-A and cancelled-adjective alternatives, leaves E/En and the cancelled qui locally doubtful, and removes the final-line stop after ens. The rightmost curve belongs to the final s of marqués; no separate terminal comma is supplied.
